speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Could you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and whether they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions flat-topped, smooth, and flesh-colored or pink, resembling small mollusks? Have you observed any central indentation or umbilication in the center of the papules?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of flesh-colored, umbilicated papules is classic for Molluscum contagiosum, especially given the daycare exposure. Since the diagnosis is clinically evident, I do not require further tests. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
